sections.hypothesis: Monday's high and low in Brisbane time set the week's direction. In weeks that break Monday's high before its low, buying the first pullback to Monday's midpoint and holding to the end of Friday makes money after costs. Monday must be special: the same measurements anchored on other weekdays must do worse.
sections.rationale: From backlog S1 (May 2025). Weakest part: no one has named who is on the other side or why the effect would persist. A possible story is that the week's first full session after the weekend sets reference levels that desks and bots watch, but that is a story, not evidence. The earlier results do not count: at least one run used a synthetic price generator built to produce the pattern (a Monday high near 26,792 when BTC traded near 84,000), and the 95.7% win rate collapsed to 24-29% once that setup was isolated. This rebuild therefore starts with a raw-effect study, and kills the idea there if Monday is not different from other days.
sections.rules: Stage 1, raw-effect study (kestrel anchor-study, 1h bars): every AEST calendar day is an anchor; its range is the day's high and low, its midpoint their average. Over the next 4 full days (for a Monday: Tuesday to Friday) record which side closes through first, and in up-first cases the return of buying the next open after the first bar whose low comes within 0.5% of the midpoint, sold at the last close. Monday is compared with the other six weekdays pooled, with 95% intervals from 2,000 resamples of whole weeks. Stage 2, strategy (monday-pullback, 1h bars, only if stage 1 survives): Monday's range is known once Monday's last bar closes; a week with a missing Monday bar is skipped. From Tuesday, the week is bullish if a bar closes above Monday's high before any closes below Monday's low. After that break (never on the breaking bar), the first bar whose low is within 0.5% of the midpoint and whose close is no more than 0.5% below it signals a long, bought at the next open. Stop: Monday's low. No target. Exit: sold at the open after Friday's last bar (AEST). At most one trade a week. Long only, risk 1% per trade (kestrel.toml).
sections.falsification: Stage 1 on BTCUSDT 1h and ETHUSDT 1h, 2020-01 to 2025-10, run once each. KILL unless, on both markets, all three hold at 95%: Monday's up-first share is above the other days'; Monday's pullback return is above the other days'; and Monday's average pullback return is above 0.22% (one round trip of fee and spread). A KILL rejects this note without running stage 2. Stage 2, only if stage 1 survives: BTCUSDT 1h and ETHUSDT 1h, 2020-01 to 2025-10, default parameters, run once each. Reject if, pooled across both markets: net expectancy after costs is 0R or below; or P(expectancy > 0) is under 90%; or fewer than 50 trades.
sections.parameters: Stage 1: tolerance 50 bps, horizon 4 days. Stage 2: tolerance_bps 50 (25-100 allowed later), exit_day 5 (Friday). The backlog's sweep (tolerance 25/50/100, stop at Monday low or 1.5 ATR, exit Friday, Sunday or trailing) is not part of this test: each variant is a trial, and sweeping on the same data is what produced the original results. It belongs in P3's walk-forward.
sections.costs: At most one trade a week, so up to about 50 a year per market and fewer in practice (only bullish weeks with a pullback). The stop sits at Monday's low, about half of Monday's range below the entry: for BTC typically 1-2.5%, so one 22 bps round trip costs roughly 0.1-0.2R. That is a real hurdle for an edge this small, which is why stage 1 checks the raw return against costs first.

history.reason: Killed before any run: the raw-effect study (kestrel anchor-study) found Monday's range no different from any other day's, which the note set as the condition for testing the strategy. Closed in the 2026-11-14 clean-out.
